parts.name: Airspeed indicator case and bezel
parts.description: United reference envelope: 3.248 in typical flange width; case depth shown at the published maximum (2.30 in ASI, 4.0 in altimeter/VSI). Unspecified diameters and features are reconstructed. Internal reference mechanisms come from separate sources; this is not a complete United replica.

sources.title: Indicator-Airspeed, United Instruments Spec. No. UI8000 (revision E)
sources.use: Best OEM exterior-envelope and operating-range source found for an actual United mechanical ASI; pair with Army Figure 4-11 only as generic internal architecture, not as the UI8000's confirmed internals.
locator: PDF p.1 states the airspeed operating principle: differential between pitot and static pressure produces the pointer indication; calibrated range for part 8000 is 0-200 mph, 8025 is 0-250 mph, and 8030 is 0-300 mph.
PDF p.7, OEM drawing: dimensioned front/side views, case per MS33549, and pitot/static port thread 1/8-27 ANPT per MIL-P-7105.

sources.title: Aviation Unit Maintenance (AVUM) and Aviation Intermediate Maintenance (AVIM) Manual for General Aircraft Maintenance, Electrical and Instrument Maintenance Procedures and Practices, Volume 4, TM 1-1500-204-23-4
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of the Army / LOGSA; hosted by Chinook Helicopter public technical-manual archive
sources.use: Best primary-source public mechanical layout for conventional ASI and VSI behavior; not a matched component overhaul manual and not usable for dimensional reconstruction.
locator: PDF p.62, printed p.4-13, Figure 4-11: sectional airspeed-indicator drawing labels static/pitot connections, diaphragm, restraining spring, hairspring, rocking shaft, sector, long lever, handstaff pinion and pointer. Adjacent text describes capsule motion converted to pointer movement by mechanical linkage.

PDF p.63, printed p.4-14, text: conventional VSI includes two air-enclosing chambers, with a pressure-sensitive diaphragm directly connected to static pressure and an airtight case connected through a thin-walled porcelain capillary; diaphragm motion drives the pointer. This is source text rather than inference.

PDF p.64, printed p.4-15, Figure 4-12: conventional VSI sectional layout with internal diaphragm/chamber, mechanical linkage and case/capillary path. It is a section/layout view, not an exploded parts drawing.
PDF p.63, printed p.4-14, Table 4-1 gives ASI test tolerance values for MS28045/MS28021/MS28046 at specified knots. Those are performance limits, not physical dimensions.
